guide: Start here: this workbook shows who does what in the house and whether it is fair. Open Settings on the Start sheet and type your household name, the children's first names and the agreed split in the yellow cells.

Replace the demo data: clear the sample rows of Chores, Chore log, Rewards, Work pattern, Laundry rota and Away-week scenario and type your own; keep the lists and settings. Grey cells calculate by themselves.

Chores: type each recurring chore with its room, frequency, minutes, default owner, effort points and the date it was last done; next due, overdue days and status calculate. Tick Paused when out of season. Intervals are typical, your own.
Chore log: type each chore done with the date, who did it and how long it took. The fairness check, the history by month and the children's points all read this one sheet.
Ranked and typed-once sheets (Cleaning Plan, Cleaning Schedule, Chore Rotation, Reward Ladder, Streaks): type the ranks or the names once and the rest fills in.
Weekly routine, Sunday: plan the meals, check the shopping list, rotate the chores with the Chore Rotation Generator, read the Cleaning Plan and glance at the calendar.
Monthly routine: pantry and freezer check, maintenance due, renewals in the next 90 days, a project check, and the household chore meeting with the Fairness Summary.
Use the 18 tools for the questions of the week: what do we clean first, who carries what, how many points to the next reward, who does the evenings on a late day, what changes if someone is away.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in; the tables with a phone column carry the links.
A single adult uses the Chores and Cleaning sheets and leaves the children's points, fairness and rotation sheets empty; the Cleaning Plan still ranks what is overdue.
Renters: read "a trade" as "a maintenance request to the landlord", and leave out the garden and exterior chores you do not own.
Fairness is a view calculated from your entries, never a verdict or an alarm: it shows the minutes and the share so that the household can talk about them.

Why a workbook: one flat price, no yearly renewal, your data stays with you, nothing to link or re-connect, no ads and no upsell. It works in Excel and Google Sheets with no macros, no add-ins and no accounts.

What this is not: not a safety service, not a reminder app, not medical, veterinary, legal or financial advice. Every date, rank and share is calculated from your entries: typical, check the manufacturer's instructions and your local rules.

listing.title: Chore Chart and Rotation Excel Template: Cleaning Schedule, Fairness Check, Laundry Rota, Kids Points and Rewards
listing.headline: See who does what at home, what is overdue and whether it is fair
listing.description:
Run the chores of your home from one Excel workbook: about 45 recurring chores by room and frequency with minutes, effort points and a default owner, a next due date and overdue days for every chore, and a weekly cleaning plan ranked most overdue first. Built for a single adult, a couple or a family, owners or renters, with a household of two adults, two children and a grandparent as the sample.

The fairness check reads your Chore log and shows each adult's minutes and points in the last 30 days, the share of the adult total against the share you agreed, and the hidden jobs (planning, booking, remembering) beside the visible ones. It is a view calculated from your entries, never an alarm. The rotation generator builds four weeks by rotation or by balancing points, with a swap cell, and the away week moves the chores of one person to the others and lists what stays unowned.

Children earn points, never money, on a reward ladder with a balance carried forward; the laundry rota shows the busiest day and the next bedding and towel change; done and missed by week, streaks and this month against the 3 complete months before it come from your own history. 18 tools answer the questions of the week: what do we clean first, who does the evening chores on a late day, how many free hours each adult has in a late-shift week, how many days to clear the overdue list, and what a swap of two chores does to the shares. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to the household, the grandparent, the babysitter, the neighbour, the dog walker and the school office.

This is part three of the eight-part Home Management suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros, no accounts and no yearly renewal, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Every date, rank and share is calculated from your entries: typical, check the manual and your local rules. It is a home kit, not a safety service, and gives no health, medical or legal advice.

Weekly cleaning plan ranked most overdue first
Fairness check with hidden jobs, a view and never an alarm
Four-week rotation by method with a swap cell
Away week: who takes the chores, what stays unowned
Children's points and a reward ladder, never money
18 tools for the questions of every week
Dashboard with 30 live figures and 22 charts
Single adults and renters can use it unchanged
No macros, no accounts, no yearly renewal
